prompt.text: Which panel shows the page's HTML structure?

hints: Its name is the plural of a page's building blocks.
cards.fullLine: The Elements panel shows the page's HTML structure.

teaching.text: Each panel answers one question; the tabs switch between them.

teaching.alt: DevTools with Elements, Console, Sources, Network and Application tabs
A beginner tour of the Chrome DevTools panels

prompt.text: panel shows logged messages and errors.

answer.text: The Console panel shows logged messages and errors.

hints: Its name comes from the text window of an old computer.
cards.fullLine: The Console panel shows logged messages and errors.

teaching.text: Start here when a page is blank: an error is often already written.

prompt.text: Which panel lists every file the page requested?

hints: It is named after the connection between browser and server.
cards.fullLine: The Network panel lists every file the page requested.

teaching.text: Each row is one request, with a status and a timing bar.

prompt.text: To pause code on a line, open the

answer.text: To pause code on a line, open the Sources panel.

hints: It is also the word for where something comes from.
cards.fullLine: To pause code on a line, open the Sources panel.

teaching.text: Breakpoints live beside the script that runs them.

prompt.text: panel shows the page's storage, cookies and cache.

answer.text: The Application panel shows the page's storage, cookies and cache.

hints: It shares its name with the program you are testing.
cards.fullLine: The Application panel shows the page's storage, cookies and cache.

teaching.text: This is where you inspect localStorage, IndexedDB and service workers.

prompt.text: Which DevTools panel records frame rate and long tasks?

hints: Its name answers the question: how fast does it feel?
cards.fullLine: The Performance panel records frame rate and long tasks.

teaching.text: A recording shows where time goes, not just how much passed.

prompt.text: Which key opens DevTools in most browsers on Windows and Linux?

hints: It is the last of the twelve function keys.
cards.fullLine: F12 opens DevTools in most browsers on Windows and Linux.

teaching.text: On a Mac, the same panel opens with the developer shortcut in the browser menu.

prompt.text: What does the device toolbar do?

answer.text: simulates screen size, pixel ratio and touch

options: simulates screen size, pixel ratio and touch
correct: simulates screen size, pixel ratio and touch

hints: It changes the frame around the page, not the page's files.
cards.fullLine: The device toolbar simulates screen size, pixel ratio and touch.

teaching.text: A simulated phone width is a preview, not a real device test.

prompt.text: The Elements panel lets you edit the

answer.text: The Elements panel lets you edit the live DOM, not the source file.

hints: The opposite of a saved file.
cards.fullLine: The Elements panel lets you edit the live DOM, not the source file.

teaching.text: Reloading the page throws those edits away.

prompt.text: Which panel shows why an image took three seconds to arrive?

hints: Look for the request's own timing bar.
cards.fullLine: The Network panel shows why an image took three seconds to arrive.

teaching.text: The timing split tells you whether the wait was the server or the download.
